summary: Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (~1885–1888). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1852–1867) and the University of Breslau (~1867–1875).
Heinrich Schenkl studied at the University of Vienna (~1878–1882). He later held academic posts at the University of Vienna (~1892–1919) and the University of Graz (~1900–1917).
Heinrich Schliemann worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in ~1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Zurich and Humboldt University of Berlin under Hirzel, Lachmann, Boeckh, Bekker, and Bopp. He was a professor at Zurich (1849, 1864–1889) and taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl (~1841–1889).

Indologist Heinrich Stönner studied at Marburg, Berlin under Geldner and Weber, and Halle under Richard Pischel. He served at the Berlin State Museums (1901) and as Indian Department Director at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1925–1931).
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1865–1876) under Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post teaching classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel studied Indology and Tibetology at Jena, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz, Strasbourg, and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller. He held a post at the University of Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying at Strasbourg, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Greifswald (1881–1901), Heidelberg University, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at SOAS, Munich under Helmut Hoffmann, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1965) and as chairholder at the University of Tübingen (1973–1998).
Heinrich von Wlislocki worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Franz Joseph University from 1875 to 1879 under Sámuel Brassai, earning a Ph.D.

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Munich under Helmut Hoffmann, and Mainz. He held posts at Saarland University, Mainz, and served as Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Kronasser was a linguist who studied at Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and Erich Frauwallner, and at Graz. He held posts at the University of Graz (1952), the University of Vienna (1953–1963), and the University of Würzburg (1963).
Indologist Heinz Kucharski studied at the University of Hamburg in 1938. He served as Director of the Indian Department at the Grassi Museum of Ethnology from ~1952 to 1974.

Heinz Mode was an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied in Berlin, Colombo, Visva-Bharati, and Basel. He held a chair in oriental archaeology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1948 to 1978.
Heinz Werner Wessler is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He was affiliated with Aarhus University (attested 1998–1999) and became a professor at Uppsala University in 2010.

Heinz Zimmermann was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Zurich, Freiburg, and Basel. He held posts at the University of Zurich (1971–1979) and was a professor of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne (1977, 1981).

Heleen De Jonckheere is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate at Ghent University. She held posts at Chicago (2021), Toronto Mississauga (2021–2024), and SOAS University of London (2022).

Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and joined the faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in ~1993.

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies, earning a PhD at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton, Griffith University, and Harvard University (from 1992).
